The test `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveOutputStreamTest.testWriteNonAsciiDirectoryNamePosixMode()` is trying to write a non-ASCII directory name to a Tar Archive. The test creates a `TarArchiveEntry` with the directory name "f\u00f6\u00f6/" and then attempts to write it using `TarArchiveOutputStream`. The problem occurs when the directory name is longer than 100 bytes, causing an exception related to writing PAX headers.

Looking at the code snippets, the `TarArchiveEntry` constructor takes the directory name as a parameter. The constructor simply sets the name without any validation or truncation logic. Then, the `TarArchiveOutputStream` constructor is called with an `OutputStream`, and it sets PAX headers for non-ASCII names.

The issue seems to be related to the handling of long directory names exceeding 100 bytes in the `TarArchiveOutputStream` implementation, specifically when writing PAX headers for non-ASCII names.

Next, I will investigate the implementation of the `TarArchiveOutputStream` constructor that sets PAX headers for non-ASCII names to identify the possible cause of the issue.
